source_scope_note: OEIS A000045; Paper I, exact polyphase reconstruction. Equality follows coefficient by coefficient from the unique division $n=3m+r$. The numerical example is finite.

title: Two Fibonacci channels share one denominator
source_scope_note: OEIS A000045. Here $B=T^2$ for $T=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\1&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. The denominator is a formal-series identity, equivalently a rational identity near zero.

title: Every Fibonacci stride has a jump recurrence
source_scope_note: OEIS A000045 and A000032, with $L_0=2$, $L_1=1$. Here $M$ is a positive integer and $m,r\ge0$. The formula follows from Cayley--Hamilton for $T^M$; the table displays strides one through six at offset one.

title: Complex phases select one residue
source_scope_note: Paper I, roots-of-unity filters; $M$ is a positive integer and $0\le r<M$. OEIS A000045 supplies the example. Exact cancellation is checked in $\mathbb Q[\zeta]/(\zeta^2+\zeta+1)$, not inferred from floating-point cancellation.

title: Refine even and odd into six coefficient streams
source_scope_note: OEIS A000045; Paper I parent--child refinement. The rows use exact values through $F_{17}$; the identity follows from splitting the parent index $m=3j+\ell$.

title: Different refinement orders reach the same coefficient
source_scope_note: Paper I refinement identity, illustrated with OEIS A000045. The two routes are exact Euclidean division; the full coefficient check uses indices zero through seventeen.

title: Three carries produce one block delay
source_scope_note: Paper I intertwining law. The matrix identity is algebraic over a polynomial ring; the displayed six-coefficient example retains its full output support.

title: Polynomial multiplication has visible residue carries
source_scope_note: Worked finite-polynomial example over the integers. The general formula follows from $r+s=M\lfloor(r+s)/M\rfloor+(r+s\bmod M)$ in a commutative coefficient ring.

title: An exponential generating function changes the weights
source_scope_note: OEIS A000045 supplies the values. Exact rational normalization; the reconstruction formula is a coefficient identity over a characteristic-zero field. It is not a claim that the channel itself is an EGF in $u$.

title: Parity separates secant and tangent counts
source_scope_note: OEIS A000111, A000364, A000182. The finite check independently divides the formal sine and cosine series and compares counts through exponent eleven.

title: Thue--Morse refines by copying and complementing
source_scope_note: OEIS A010060, offset zero. $t(n)$ is the binary digit sum modulo two. The universal recurrence follows by appending a binary zero or one; exact checks cover $0\le n<256$.

title: Binary weight keeps the affine increment
source_scope_note: OEIS A000120, offset zero. The recurrence and generating identity follow from binary appending. Exact checks cover $0\le n<256$; the bars display only parents zero through seven.

title: A Haar bank preserves average and detail together
source_scope_note: Exact Haar two-channel teaching example over $\mathbb R$; amplitudes lie in $\mathbb Q(\sqrt2)$. The plotted bars are numerical renderings of the stated exact algebraic values.

title: One retained channel cannot identify the original
source_scope_note: Explicit finite counterexample over the integers. This proves noninjectivity of retaining only the even channel, rather than estimating reconstruction quality on a sample.

title: A complete operation agrees along both routes
source_scope_note: Paper I intertwining, worked on a finite prefix of OEIS A000045. The universal matrix identity follows from the two-phase carry; exact integer checks retain the whole output polynomial.

title: Read a tap as a delayed contribution
source_scope_note: New worked FIR example. Integer indices $n\ge0$; every input is zero at negative indices. The finite tap list has length $L=3$. This convention applies throughout the tap atlas.

title: Execute the taps on Fibonacci numbers
source_scope_note: Fibonacci convention $F_0=0,F_1=1$; OEIS A000045 as verified in the sequence atlas. New tap example. Indices $0$--$11$; exact inputs and outputs are recorded in \texttt{evidence/tap\_checks.json}.

title: Turn three taps into a two-phase matrix
source_scope_note: PSC Paper V, Theorem 4.2 and Corollary 4.5, specialized to $M=2$ and $h=(1,2,1)$; new exact derivation. Rows are output phases, columns are input phases. Causal zero extension fixes the initial positions.

title: Locate the delay when a tap wraps a block
source_scope_note: PSC Paper V, Theorem 4.2. New per-tap expansion of the matrix in T03. The labels $E_m,O_m$ denote phase coefficients, while $E(u),O(u)$ denote their OGFs.

title: Route a finite filter through four phases
source_scope_note: PSC Paper V, Theorem 4.2, Corollary 4.5, and Example 4.6. The plotted matrix uses $M=4,L=5$. Exact routing also checked for moduli $2$--$6$ and tap lengths $1$--$9$; these finite tests verify the implementation.

title: Compose filters before or after phase splitting
source_scope_note: PSC Paper V, Proposition 4.4 and Corollary 4.5; new signed-filter example. The rightmost matrix acts first. Exact polynomial convolution and exact matrix multiplication agree in the check ledger.

title: Use signed taps as finite differences
source_scope_note: New exact finite-difference example, tap list $(1,-1)$, input $x[n]=n^2$ for $n\ge0$. Indices $0$--$10$ checked exactly. This lesson does not claim a finite constant-coefficient annihilator for arbitrary sequences.

title: Let recurrence taps expose initial data
source_scope_note: Fibonacci recurrence with causal zero extension; new tap presentation. Twenty-four coefficients checked exactly. The polynomial $1-z-z^2$ uses the fine-delay variable $z$, unlike the coarse variable $u$ in T09.

title: Give the two Fibonacci phases different numerators
source_scope_note: Fibonacci phase extraction and exact recurrence calculation. Twenty-four coefficients in each channel checked. Residual notation: $\delta_1$ and $\delta_0-\delta_1$ on the coarse index.

title: Separate finite taps from an infinite reciprocal response
source_scope_note: New formal-OGF reconstruction of T09. Twenty-four coefficients checked exactly. The reciprocal identity is formal around $u=0$; the plate makes no claim about convergence at every complex value of $u$.

title: Read frequency response from the tap polynomial
source_scope_note: New FIR frequency example. NumPy complex128 on 801 samples of $[0,\pi]$. The endpoint and DC identities are algebraic; the sampled error is recorded separately. No ideal anti-aliasing claim is made.

title: Expose the delay carried by symmetric taps
source_scope_note: New symmetric FIR example. The displayed formula is exact. The numerical phase check uses 801 interior samples and excludes $\pm\pi$. A phase value supplied by floating-point arithmetic at a zero is not used as evidence.

title: Reconstruct exactly with Haar analysis and synthesis
source_scope_note: Standard Haar pair transform, independently verified by direct matrix algebra. Exact sum/difference witnesses cover all 121 integer pairs in $[-5,5]^2$, with the common square-root factor canceled symbolically.

title: Reverse signed prediction and update steps
source_scope_note: New exact lifting example over rational coefficients. Negative coarse indices are zero in both directions. Sixteen signed filter-pair witnesses checked with integers and fractions. Streaming use must retain the histories needed by both filters.

title: Resample at rate three over two by exact routing
source_scope_note: New small-filter $3/2$ example. Exact zero insertion, convolution, downsampling, and phase routing agree. The filter demonstrates indexing only; no passband, stopband, or alias-suppression specification is claimed.

title: Carry the needed state across chunk boundaries
source_scope_note: New direct-form FIR streaming example. Twenty signed-filter cases cover lengths $1$--$5$, four chunk partitions, and complete flushed tails. The $L-1$ rule describes this implementation, rather than a universal lower bound on every filter realization.

title: Seeds choose which modes survive
source_scope_note: New elementary rational-series example, $n\ge0$. Numerator residuals and all three mode formulas are checked through index eighteen. Cancellations are exact; this is not a robustness claim for perturbed seeds or hidden states.

title: Compile taps against an exact recurrence
source_scope_note: OEIS A000045, $F_0=0,F_1=1$, with new exact polynomial algebra. The coefficient check runs through index eighteen; finite-input tails are checked with $N=DF$, including terminal residuals. The reduction is for this recurrence input; it does not replace the original filter on arbitrary signals.

title: A formal reciprocal need not be a stable filter
source_scope_note: New causal geometric-response examples, $n\ge0$, with zero input at negative indices. Exact rational convolutions checked through index eighteen. The unstable rational expression can be evaluated on the unit circle, but its causal Fourier series there does not converge.

title: Coefficient division becomes an area average
source_scope_note: OEIS A000984 and A000108; new elementary integral derivation. The square-root branch equals one at zero, $C(0)=1$ by removal, and the analytic identities hold on $|z|<1/4$. Coefficient identities also hold over formal rational series; exact checks cover indices zero through eighteen.

title: Transport the operator with the normalization
source_scope_note: Exact formal coefficient identity over $\mathbb Q$, $\mathbb R$, or $\mathbb C$; $n,K\ge0$ are integers and $h_0,\ldots,h_K$ are finite taps. Counts transported in the opposite direction use $NHN^{-1}$ with weights $h_k/(n)_k$ for $n\ge k$. Prefixes are not finite input cutoffs.

title: Bernoulli resolves a discrete antiderivative
source_scope_note: Bernoulli-polynomial normalization from Paper I and sequence lesson S11, with $B_1=-1/2$. Expanding the stated polynomial proves its difference identity for every real or complex $x$; telescoping proves the integer sum. Exact sample checks cover $0\le N\le50$.

title: The boundary changes what an inverse can recover
source_scope_note: Exact four-periodic linear algebra over $\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb R$. In the causal panel each four-value vector is zero outside indices $0$--$3$; adding five affects those stored values only. Equal periodic differences force a constant difference, while telescoping gives the zero-sum condition.

title: A finite record leaves endpoint impulses
source_scope_note: Direct coefficient derivation, $P_N=\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}F_nz^n$, $F_0=0,F_1=1$. OEIS A000045 supplies the record. Exact finite checks cover $N=2$--$20$; the displayed general identity follows by collecting coefficients, not by extrapolating those checks.

title: Transfer the whole residual into three channels
source_scope_note: Direct carry calculation, $A(C_3)=I-C_3-C_3^2$, with $u=z^3$ under synthesis. Exact integer polynomial arithmetic checks the complete three-channel result and all ten synthesized output coefficients. No channel is discarded.

title: An interior perturbation has its own signature
source_scope_note: Exact one-sample perturbation experiment over the integers. The identity follows by linearity of multiplication by $A(z)$. This example identifies the consequences of its specified change; an arbitrary residual alone does not decide whether data or an assumed recurrence model is wrong.

title: A discarded channel returns through the next operation
source_scope_note: Explicit finite counterexample, with $u=z^2$ under synthesis: no map $U$ on even input channels can satisfy $\mathcal R_{2,0}(A(z)P)=U(\mathcal R_{2,0}P)$ for every finite integer polynomial $P$. Equal arguments would force equal values. This does not rule out recovery under an additional model.

title: Repair with a declared recurrence model
source_scope_note: Direct finite-state derivation: the even values are $(a,a+b,2a+3b,5a+8b)$. The two checks are necessary and sufficient for a unique completion inside this length-eight recurrence family. Exact tests cover 49 integer seed pairs and 196 inconsistent observation cases. No claim of recovery for arbitrary records or noisy observations is made.

title: Keep the history and the phase clock
source_scope_note: Exact direct-form streaming and output routing, with zero history initially. All 128 positive chunk compositions of this eight-value record are checked against whole-record convolution and routing, including the two-zero flush. The stated history describes this implementation; resetting the phase clock changes output addresses even if the arithmetic samples remain correct.
